memos.risk:
Risk officer call: this is a refuse, not a sized trade.

Reasons from the brief:
- The coin is down 65% from its 30-minute high and 65% over 30 minutes, with net outflow of 6.16 SOL in the last 15 minutes. Momentum is broken, and most coins never recover a dip like this.
- Post-graduation launch-bot activity is present, with a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.17 and the top 5 buyers holding 41% of early flow. That looks like a decaying bot-driven pump, not organic demand.
- Pool depth is 53.6 SOL, so a $20 round trip would carry meaningful impact and fees on top of an already-negative base rate.
- The "ORGANIC" label and the name are data, not reassurance. Neither offsets the flow.

Refuse any size. If the desk wants a rule for next time: no entry while the coin is in a net-outflow trend with bot-heavy early flow, regardless of class label.
memos.scout:
Honest case FOR buying: limited. The coin is alive, has 443 buyers and a fairly broad curve (top-3 share 8.6%, bundle share 13.6%, no airdrop dump seen), so it isn't obviously a factory or operator-run launch. Buyers outnumbered sellers in the first two minutes after graduation (89 buyers, 26.4 SOL, sell/buy ratio 1.17 meaning sells were heavier, so that's a weak point). The last 15 minutes show real activity: 40 buyers and 10.96 SOL of buys, about $3.3k volume.

But the demand case fails on the key test. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is -6.16 SOL, sellers (43) outnumber buyers (40), the price is down 20% in that window and 65% off its 30-minute high. Sell pressure exceeds buy pressure now, not just historically. Nothing in the brief shows demand that will persist for 30-60 minutes. The 5 largest post-graduation buyers hold 40% of early buying, and a launch bot was present. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and no sign of a reversal, I see no honest case to buy. Recommend SKIP.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a slow bleed, not a sudden rug. The coin is down 64.7% from its 30-minute high with a 64.8% drawdown, and in the last 15 minutes sellers (43) outnumbered buyers (40) and net flow was -6.16 SOL, with sell volume (17.12 SOL) well above buy volume (10.96 SOL). The first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.17, a launch bot present, and the top 5 buyers holding 40.5% of early buying, which points to early insiders taking profit into retail demand. Bundle share (13.6%) and completer share (19.7%) add some sniper and insider concentration. With a 53.6 SOL pool and a $20 ticket, round-trip fees of 1.4-5.1% are a meaningful hurdle against any bounce. Trend and flow both point down, so skip.
